modules.title: First boot and bounded input
modules.description: Read the boot guide, distinguish host models from a native kernel, and handle input without crossing its bounds.

modules.title: Firmware, services and storage
modules.description: Follow firmware reservations, system calls, file operations and ownership.

modules.title: Memory boundaries and diagnostics
modules.description: Inspect bounded file ranges, discover native contracts and read timers without allocating diagnostic storage.

modules.title: Project: a physical frame inventory
modules.description: Reserve, allocate and release modeled frames with explicit exhaustion and overflow checks.

modules.title: Project: task scheduling
modules.description: Trace ready, running and waiting states, cancellation and task identity.

modules.title: Project: storage writeback
modules.description: Separate staged bytes from stable bytes, budget flushes and validate a complete imported image.

modules.title: Project: an asynchronous device queue
modules.description: Prepare requests, publish them, check completion ownership and wait for reset acknowledgement.

modules.title: Project: a system-call boundary
modules.description: Check rights, revisions, text and capacity before publishing an event and its reply.

modules.title: Laboratory: protect the user-memory boundary
modules.description: Begin with virtual addresses and page ownership. Follow preflight and copying, then study refusal tests, cleanup and the difference between a host model and a booted guest.

modules.title: Laboratory: validate a boot handoff
modules.description: Read bytes, bound counts, validate memory ownership and publish a complete observation. Continue into firmware descriptors and freestanding qualification without changing the existing boot path.

modules.title: From a booted kernel to observable services
Laboratory: produce a validated boot handoff
modules.description: Encode through the production Kernel writer, inspect narrowing and ownership, and qualify bytes independently of the reader.

modules.title: Laboratory: own aligned contiguous physical pages
modules.description: Use the production Kernel allocator to understand absolute alignment, fragmented capacity and complete release, then separate host bookkeeping from platform evidence.

modules.title: Trace normal startup, output and recovery
modules.description: Follow the real Kernel coordinator, distinguish image purposes, preserve output ownership and qualify exact recovery decisions.

modules.title: Bind native guest and storage evidence
modules.description: Identify the tested sources and images, then separate disposable writes from fresh readback.

modules.title: Bounded packet admission
modules.description: Read synthetic Ethernet/IPv4 captures and distinguish parser checks from a working network device.

modules.title: Execute packet admission in the diagnostic guest
modules.description: Move bounded packet observations into a freestanding image and require complete ordered execution evidence.

modules.title: Guest runtime and source grammar boundary
modules.description: Keep source-level compiler features separate from freestanding execution and include both in honest qualification.

modules.title: Configuration and guest identity
modules.description: Connect host input observations with independent RISC-V artifacts and complete guest outcomes.

modules.title: UDP capture admission and guest evidence
modules.description: Extend the existing native packet reader with explicit transport policy, exact lengths and real diagnostic-guest checks.

modules.title: Caller output ownership and device lifetime
modules.description: Trace the real block driver, reproduce output aliasing and distinguish host fault injection from named virtual-device evidence.

modules.title: Private VM locals in user mode
modules.description: Connect bounded integer storage to real user-process execution and build-fixture evidence.

modules.title: Forward VM paths in user mode
modules.description: Exercise branch fuel, malformed joins and process ownership through the shared freestanding runtime.
